plane_fold.mathematics: After the two perpendicular half-folds, the four corners of the quarter-sheet represent: an original corner,A(four clipped outer corners); an edge-fold corner,B(two opposite top/bottom V-notches); the other edge-fold corner,D(two opposite left/right V-notches); or the center,C(a central diamond). Unfolding reflects a single corner-cut oblique segment horizontally and vertically. Every new cut edge is oblique to the original sheet edges; the square hole in E has horizontal/vertical cut edges and cannot arise. Thus E uniquely fails; the four realizable classes A/B/C/D are all displayed.

plane_fold.mathematics: A convex vertex on the union outline of two triangular cards must be a visible original card vertex; a transverse intersection of two card edges is concave for their union, not convex. Every original card vertex is60degrees. E has four convex90degree corners, so it is impossible. A is the union of an upward side2 triangle with base[(-1,0),(1,0)] and a downward side2 triangle with base[(-1,2.0784609690826525),(1,2.0784609690826525)]. B is two side2 equilateral triangles on opposite sides of the shared segment[(5,0),(5,2)]. C is the union of right-pointing triangles[(10,0),(10,2),(11.732050807568877,1)] and its translation[1.0392304845413263,0]. D uses[(15,0),(15,2),(16.732050807568877,1)] and left-pointing[(16.732050807568877,0.5),(16.732050807568877,2.5),(15,1.5)]. Hence A/B/C/D are realizable and E uniquely not.
